attempted_claim: Let W_a be the affine Weyl group of type tilde{F}_4 with equal parameters. Using the diagrammatic Soergel-bimodule categorification of its Hecke algebra, let {{}^p b_w} denote the p-canonical basis (p=0 or prime, p=0 meaning the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis). Determine explicitly the partition of W_a into Kazhdan-Lusztig two-sided cells by a finite set of representatives or a decidable alcove-combinatorial membership criterion, and for each prime p the coarsening/refinement given by the p-canonical two-sided cells; in particular decide whether the two partitions coincide for all p and, if not, identify the smallest prime at which a Kazhdan-Lusztig two-sided cell splits and describe the splitting.
decisive_failure: No complete or original auditable mathematical result was established: the exact infinite-cell partition, the all-primes p-canonical comparison, and the smallest splitting prime all remain open. Bounded enumerations and general p-cell theory were insufficient, and no emergent finding meeting the originality and value standard was discovered.
